summary: The note describes how schools are adopting data analytics to track student performance and personalize learning, a trend called Precision Education. It gives examples from several schools and vendors, including real-time monitoring, dropout prediction, engagement tracking, and continuous feedback loops. It also covers ethical concerns about student privacy and the value of preparing students for a data-driven world.
one_line: Schools are adopting data analytics for personalized, real-time tracking of student performance, raising privacy questions while promising better engagement and outcomes.
key_facts: On October 7, 2023, Stonewall Collegiate Institute announced a data analytics system to monitor student engagement and performance in real-time.
Madeline Grant, director of technology integration at Stonewall Collegiate Institute, said the system allows the school to respond to student needs "with unprecedented precision."
Precision Education is likened to precision medicine and uses data to create a personalized learning trajectory for each student.
On September 15, 2023, ARIES Educational Solutions unveiled in Chicago a tool that predicts high school dropout risk with a reported 90 percent accuracy.
Dr. Emily Rutherford, chief data scientist at ARIES, said the algorithms are not about reducing students to numbers but about delivering insights for a more engaged student experience.

Greenwood Academy, in the suburbs of San Francisco, began integrating data analytics into its pedagogy in early September 2023; Principal James Peterson said teachers have dashboards giving a 360-degree view of each student.

Bright Horizons Academy in Austin, Texas, began using engagement tracking software after September 2023, tracking class discussion participation, assignment submission, and digital textbook interactions.
Victoria Lee, a senior teacher at Bright Horizons, said engagement can now be quantified, understood, and improved.

On November 12, 2023, the National Education Association held a summit that proposed a framework for ethical data use, including anonymization of student records and stringent data security protocols.
Privacy advocate Jordan Michaels said student information must be protected and that the potential of these tools must be balanced against responsibility to students.
Overland Tech High School in Orlando, Florida, introduced continuous analytic feedback loops in December 2023; math teacher Eric Cho said he can adjust teaching almost daily.
Tech correspondent Liam Wright, in an article dated December 1, 2023, argued that acclimatizing students to a data-rich environment is essential for their future roles.
